findings.claim: The new z.ai quota GET builds a default ureq agent (follows up to 5 redirects) with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` attached, so a redirect from api.z.ai would be followed — unlike maintain/env.rs, which pins redirects(0) and re-targets by hand, same-site only, for keyless GETs; the wave's stated invariant is that a request carrying an API key never follows a redirect.
findings.trigger: api.z.ai (or an intermediary) answering GET /api/monitor/usage/quota/limit with a 3xx to another host while the ZAI key is set.

evidence.observation: Both build `ureq::AgentBuilder::new().timeout(HTTP_TIMEOUT).build()` with no redirects(0) and send the bearer token; contrast crates/c3/src/maintain/env.rs:122-157 which sets .redirects(0) and follows only keyless GETs, max 3 hops, same site.
Not verified whether ureq's default strips Authorization on cross-host redirects; the follow itself is certain.

findings.verification: Inspect the vendored ureq 2.12.1 source (redirect_auth_headers default) or point the ZAI env key at a local server that 302s cross-host and observe whether the Authorization header arrives.
findings.remedy: Build the agent with .redirects(0) (and treat a 3xx as no data) in zai_get and kimi_get, matching the maintain env policy.

findings.claim: When the installed version cannot be parsed (`installed = None`, text "unknown"), the pass still updates and, on a post-update smoke failure, rolls back to the literal string "unknown" (npm install -g @openai/codex@unknown, grok update --version unknown), which cannot succeed — the engine is left on the version that failed its smoke although a rollback path existed.
findings.trigger: A CLI whose `--version` output stops parsing (format change across versions is exactly when this happens) plus an available update whose post-update smoke fails.

evidence.observation: The up-to-date check is inside `if let Some(inst) = installed`, so None falls through to update with installed_text="unknown"; do_rollback receives installed_text verbatim.

findings.verification: Point CODEX_CONSULT_GROK_EXE at a fake whose --version prints no version token, latest > installed, smoke pass-then-fail: the pass reports "rollback failed" and the engine stays on the new version.
findings.remedy: Hold the update (report "installed version unknown") whenever `installed` is None for an engine with a rollback path.

findings.claim: The model step ignores both the `--engine` filter and C3_MAINTAIN_SKIP: `c3 maintain --run --engine codex` still collects and swaps models of grok/agy/claude seats, editing the roster and spending smoke turns outside the scope the operator selected.
findings.trigger: Any scoped or skip-configured pass (`--engine codex` or C3_MAINTAIN_SKIP=grok) with a roster seat whose source has a successor.

evidence.observation: run_models receives `opts` but reads only opts.dry_run; `skip` and `only` are computed in pass_inner and never passed to it.

findings.verification: With a roster holding a swappable grok seat, run `c3 maintain --run --dry-run --engine codex` and observe grok model candidate lines in the output.
findings.remedy: Filter swap candidates (and collect sources) by opts.engines and skip_set inside run_models.

findings.claim: A model-swap smoke builds its Target directly from the candidate instead of going through pick_target, so the saturation guard (no plan whose governing window is at 90 %+ used) and the budget-headroom/codex-custom-provider preference never apply to swap smokes — they can spend quota on an exhausted plan.
findings.trigger: A swap candidate exists on a seat whose plan window is at or beyond 90 % used at pass time.

evidence.observation: The saturation check and ranking exist only inside pick_target; the swap path constructs Target { provider, model } inline and calls run_one_smoke directly.

findings.verification: Set the seat's plan snapshot to 95 % used, offer a successor id, and run a non-dry pass: the smoke runs anyway.
findings.remedy: Route the swap target through pick_target's plan_headroom check (or skip the swap when the seat's plan is saturated).

findings.claim: The dead-re-ask salvage concatenates ALL text events, so the reply recorded for a run whose re-ask read and then died can still contain the interim placeholder written before the last tool call — inconsistent with grok_turn_outcome's final-text-after-last-tool-call rule the same change introduces.
findings.trigger: A grok re-ask that emits an answer-shaped interim note, makes tool calls, emits partial final text, then dies.

evidence.observation: grok_salvage pushes every `text` event; the outcome path keeps only final_text after the last tool_call.

findings.verification: Script a grok re-ask (fake stream) with a placeholder, a tool_call, then partial text and no end event: the .reply.json contains both the placeholder and the partial text.
findings.remedy: Make grok_salvage return the text after the last tool_call (fall back to all text only when there was none).

findings.claim: The in-use guard is a one-shot match of process names against the launcher's file stem, checked before two smokes that take minutes: npm-shimmed CLIs may run under a different image name (node / codex-<target>) so a live consultation may not be detected, and there is a TOCTOU window between the check and do_update.
findings.trigger: A consultation on the engine starts while the pass is running its pre-update smoke, or the engine's real process name differs from the launcher stem.

evidence.observation: engine_in_use compares lowercased process-name stems; it runs once per engine before maintain_one_engine, which then smokes twice before updating.
Windows npm shims (.cmd) launch the package binary whose image name may not equal the shim stem; consequence is bounded (Windows file locks make the update fail cleanly; POSIX keeps the old inode).

findings.verification: Start a real `c3 consult --engine grok` and, while it runs, run `c3 maintain --run --engine grok` in a sandbox: check whether the pass reports "skipped: in use".
findings.remedy: Re-check engine_in_use immediately before do_update, and match on the launcher's resolved binary path as well as the stem.

findings.claim: apply_swap writes the roster with a bare fs::write (no temp+rename), so a crash mid-write can leave a truncated roster file; the same-day .bak-maintain-<date> backup stands, but recovery is manual. Separately, two seats sharing the same provider AND model value can never be swapped (replace_entry_model returns an ambiguity error) — safe, but a silent no-op.
findings.trigger: Power loss / kill during the roster write; or a roster with duplicate provider+model seats offered a successor.

evidence.observation: State files use tmp+rename (mod.rs:94-107) but the roster write does not; the disambiguation filter keeps every match when both entries name the provider.

findings.verification: Kill the process between the backup and the write (or construct duplicate seats) and inspect the roster / the pass report.
findings.remedy: Write the roster via temp file + rename like write_state; consider disambiguating duplicate seats by position.

reply_markdown:
**Verdict: ACCEPT** — no path found that damages a machine, a roster or a consultation record; seven minor follow-ups below.

**Q1.** The order smoke-installed → update → re-read → smoke → rollback (`maintain/mod.rs:549-595`) has no install-without-smoke path; dry-run takes no lock and writes nothing (tested). Defects: (a) with an unparsable installed version the pass updates and then "rolls back" to the literal `unknown`, which must fail — engine left on the smoke-failed version though a pin existed (finding #2); (b) the model step ignores `--engine` and `C3_MAINTAIN_SKIP` (finding #3). In-use: guard exists but is a one-shot stem match with a minutes-long TOCTOU window (finding #6). No hook loop: a pass writes `next_due` even when everything is held (`mod.rs:454-462`); a crash mid-pass leaves `next_due` stale so each new session spawns one retry pass (bounded smoke re-spend). Crash consistency: state is tmp+rename atomic, stale locks are taken over by dead-pid check (`mod.rs:216-258`) — sound.

**Q2.** `replace_entry_model` replaces exactly one value range, disambiguated by provider, errors on zero/ambiguous matches (`models.rs:264-296`); the result is re-validated through `validate_roster` before any write (`models.rs:243-253`), so a hostile model id that breaks JSON writes nothing. Backup once per day, taken before the first edit (`models.rs:237-241`). The successor rule (same prefix+suffix, same major, higher minor, `version.rs:156-177`) and the stamp rule (`version.rs:144-149`) are conservative and sound: stamped, major-jump and new-family ids are announce-only. Two seats sharing provider+model can never swap (ambiguity error — safe direction). The roster write is a bare non-atomic `fs::write` (`models.rs:254`, finding #7).

**Q3.** Version strings reaching commands are strictly `[0-9.]+` (`version.rs:62-81`), so `npm install -g @openai/codex@<v>`, `grok update --version <v>` and `KIMI_VERSION` cannot carry metacharacters; model ids travel only as argv, validated JSON values and the bounded (400-char) report line. Kimi installer: https-only, hand-followed redirects capped at 3 and same-site (`env.rs:115-190`), no signature check beyond TLS+vendor domain (by design). Endpoint model-list GETs carry the key with `follow_redirects=false` (`models.rs:126-143`). Gap: the new z.ai quota GET uses ureq's default agent — which follows up to 5 redirects — with the bearer key attached (`budget/mod.rs` `zai_get`), contradicting the wave's own key-redirect invariant (finding #1; the pre-existing `kimi_get` shares it). Children get scrubbed host markers (`env.rs:93`).

**Q4.** Well covered. Zero-tool non-raw replies always hit the guard; a rescue records the re-ask's own session (`secondary.rs:1429-1445`); all-fail and dead paths record no thread for grok, so an abandoned thread is never resumed (`secondary.rs:1507-1518`); the reply file follows salvage/`raw_text`, and `structured` cannot re-select the placeholder because it is gated on `usable` (`orchestrate/mod.rs:4786`). Integration tests pin each behaviour. One inconsistency: dead-run salvage concatenates all text events (`grok.rs:740-762`), so an interim placeholder can still appear in a dead run's recorded reply (finding #5).

**Q5.** Parsing is fixture-verified for both sources; percent→ratio /100, epoch-ms resets, elapsed from reset time; failure or a null allowance yields no windows so the snapshot applies. No wrong-window path found beyond finding #1.

**Q6. Untested:** the kimi update path (installer download/run/pin) has no test at all; no end-to-end model swap against a real roster (every maintain test sets `C3_MAINTAIN_MODELS=off`); the in-use skip and lock contention/stale takeover; the z.ai/muse live fetches and their fall-through to snapshot (the network seam is not injectable in budget); no integration assertion that grok argv now omits `--json-schema` (and passes it under `--schema-transport native`); the Windows detached spawn is only tested negatively.
